answers.rationale: Her history supports a conditional, site-specific approach rather than a fixed no-car rule: for early Cary workshops with uncertain visitor parking, she held a cancellable compact pending parking confirmation. The north-side early starts, demo materials, downtown dinner, and unknown parking similarly justify a cancellable hold and rideshare comparison.

This is a fixed-site, short downtown trip with very high parking cost and no confirmed offsite work. Her prior plans treat downtown cars as unnecessary while retaining a conditional fallback if offsite movement appears; transit or rideshare is sufficient for the airport and Capitol Hill dinner.

Her St. Pete family trip shows that she will add a pay-later, cancellable car when groceries, storms, booster logistics, and flexible offsite plans make it useful, even after initially favoring no car. Here, the zoo, La Jolla, grocery stop, possible rain, and booster make a cancellable compact the calibrated choice after checking parking.

Her transfer choices are contextual: she has used rail as a primary option when it is direct and practical, while retaining rideshare for weather, delays, fatigue, or poor conditions. With a carry-on, no time pressure, station-adjacent hotel, and likely afternoon surge, Link should be primary with rideshare as the fallback.
